title: Chamber Media vs AI Video Ads: Cost and Performance Compared
summary: Chamber Media vs AI video ads on cost and performance: Chamber's published minimum, AI video prices and the testing setup behind results. Checked October 2026.
body_markdown:
## How do the cost structures differ?


Chamber charges a monthly fee that grows with the team and the account. AI providers charge for finished output, so cost follows volume and format. The gap shows up when you count what each fee buys. Chamber does not publish how many ads its minimum covers, so you cannot divide its fee by a count. Vidful and AI Vidia do publish counts. Dividing Vidful's $3,495 across 60 videos gives about $58 each, and AI Vidia's €8,500 across 40 videos gives roughly €213 each. Both figures are our simple arithmetic and exclude media spend.


Note the scale. The low end of Chamber's range is larger than Vidful's whole 60-video plan, but Chamber's fee also covers strategy and management, which Vidful does not say it provides. That is why the comparison has to hold scope fixed: price the same number of finished ads, then price the testing and media separately.


Before you compare, confirm three things in writing: the revision rounds, the usage rights, and whether the price includes the launch. Revision rounds often decide the real cost more than the headline fee does. Chamber's terms are month-to-month, but its minimum applies every month you stay. Vidful bills monthly with no contracts and CreatStrat says you can cancel anytime, so a short test costs less to walk away from.


## What does performance depend on, and what can you verify?


Neither Chamber nor the AI providers publish results we could verify on the pages we checked, so this comparison cannot rank performance. What you can check is the setup behind results. Whoever makes your ads, Meta's[video ads guide](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads-guide/video) is the baseline: it lists a 4:5 ratio at 1440 x 1800 pixels for Feed video, and every placement you buy needs its own cut.


[Pilothouse](https://www.pilothouse.co/post/meta-creative-testing-framework-the-3-3-3-approach-to-finding-winners) , a Meta ads agency for DTC brands, describes a 3-3-3 testing framework on its blog: three funnel levels, three angles and three formats, tested in equal-budget ad sets before winners move into Advantage+ sales campaigns. Use a structure like that as a checklist for either option:


- How many distinct concepts arrive each month, and how do they differ in angle, not just wording?
- How is each concept tested, and with what budget per ad set?
- Who moves the winners into scale, and who retires the losers?
- Which result decides a winner: cost per purchase, cost per lead, or something earlier in the funnel?


Chamber's Facebook page describes matrix testing, so ask how its matrix is built. Ask AI providers the same questions about concepts per month and test design. For a deeper method, see our[ad creative testing](https://knowlify.com/articles/ad-creative-testing) guide.


A fair head-to-head is simple to run. Give both options the same brief, the same placements and the same budget, then compare cost per result over the same window. Anything else mixes creative quality with offer, audience and timing.


## Which buyer should pick which option?


Chamber fits a brand that wants one team for creative and media, and whose budget clears its published thresholds. It also fits a brand that wants live-action production or long-form video for YouTube and connected TV. The[Chamber Media alternatives](https://knowlify.com/articles/chamber-media-alternatives) guide compares other options by scope.


AI video services fit a brand that already runs media, or has a media buyer, and needs a steady supply of finished ads. Knowlify fits that second group, with optional Meta management if you want it. The two are not exclusive: you can keep an agency for media and add a separate supply of AI-made ads for volume.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for weekly AI video ads, with optional Meta management, plans from $5,000 a month and a 90-day guarantee (terms on the site). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month.
- Chamber's published minimum is around $5K to $10K a month for creative, strategy and management, with media spend on top.
- AI video providers publish output-based prices, so compare cost per finished ad after revisions and before media.
- Neither side publishes verifiable performance results, so judge the testing plan and the number of distinct concepts per month.
- If you need live-action production or ads off Meta, choose a provider built for that job.


## FAQ


### Does Chamber Media publish its prices?


Partly. Its FAQ says to expect around $5K to $10K a month at minimum for creative development, strategy and management, with media spend on top. The pages we checked do not publish a per-ad rate, so ask for one in writing.


### Is Knowlify cheaper than Chamber Media?


We cannot say from published numbers. Knowlify's plans start at $5,000 a month, while Chamber publishes a $5K to $10K monthly minimum. Ask both for a quote on the same number of finished ads, and ask Knowlify for a creative-only price if you already have a media buyer.


### Do AI video ads perform as well as live-action?


We did not test output or results, so we cannot rank them. Judge both options with the same brief, the same placements and the same budget, and compare cost per result. In our view, a studio suits one polished piece or real people on camera, while testing needs several distinct concepts, so the deciding factor is concepts per month and test design rather than AI versus live-action.


### What should a quote include?


Ask for the number of finished ads, the formats and aspect ratios, the revision rounds, the usage rights and whether the launch is included. Those five items make two quotes comparable, whichever type of provider sends them.
